A mostly easy trail that starts near Bluffers Park's West Change Rooms, then winds  its way around most of Bluffers Park towards the beach at the east side.  It then continues east along a hard-packed dirt trail just  inland of the beach. Muddy in spots, but not too bad. Hiking boots were an asset.  Eventually the sand beach and dirt trail merge into a narrow stony beach, here hiking boots were essential.  The stony beach narrows to almost nothing, with the Bluffs falling into the water at a near 90 degree angle.  I can easily see the west end of the Guildwood Shoreline Trail that i hiked a few days ago, perhaps 200 metres away.  But as I mentioned then, to traverse that gap I would need to be either a duck or a boat.  

The steep Bluffs are probably supplying sand to a longshore current, which sustains the amazing beach.   Which was packed with thousands of people and dozens of swimmers enjoying the hazy warm summer day.  Lots of families were picnicing on the beach and the grassy central trail.  Despite this, the beach and park were amazingly tidy, nearly zero litter.  Great to see.  The Blue Flag was up, indicating that the water was tested today and is safe to swim in.

Weekday parking is free until 5pm.  Which I did not discover until reading the sign a
*after* I paid.  City of Toronto: you are welcome.   Can't really begrudge contributing to a well-used, beautiful facility.
